setup: Two hex dumbbells, shoulder width apart
High plank, hands on the handles
execution: Brace like a plank, hips level
Row one dumbbell to your hip
Set it down softly, then switch
Push the other hand into the floor
faults: Don't twist your hips to lift
Don't let your hips sag or pike
Don't drop the dumbbell back down

notes: Use hex dumbbells that sit flat; round ones can roll under your hand and wrist.
A wider foot stance makes it easier to keep the hips level. Start light; the trunk limits the load, not the back.
Keep the wrists straight over the handles.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Kneeling renegade row
regressions.reason: Knees down shortens the lever so the row is easier to control.

regressions.name: Plank
regressions.reason: Build the plank hold before lifting a hand.

progressions.reason: A push-up between rows adds pressing work.

progressions.reason: Feet closer together makes it harder to stay square.

substitutions.reason: Same row with bench support, so you can go heavier.

substitutions.name: Three-point dumbbell row
substitutions.reason: One-arm row with some trunk demand but a stable base.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Anti-rotation core work without the row.

substitutions.name: Bear crawl

guideBrief.cameraNote: View from in front of the head, camera a little above shoulder height, so the level hips and the rowing elbow are both visible. Dumbbells on the floor under the shoulders.

keyPositions.label: Plank
keyPositions.describe: High plank on two hex dumbbells under the shoulders, arms straight. Feet wider than hip width, body straight from head to heels, hips level.

keyPositions.label: Row
keyPositions.describe: One dumbbell rowed up beside the lower ribs, elbow close to the side. Other arm straight and pushing into its dumbbell. Hips still level and square to the floor.

ikHints: Supporting hand and both feet stay fixed
Hips stay level with the floor
emphasise: Hips stay level while one hand lifts
Wide feet for a stable base
doNotShow: Dumbbell dropped back to the floor

uncertain.note: Filed as core (the expansion research groups it with core work). It is also a horizontal pull; Ben may prefer horizontal_pull.
Hex dumbbells come from the expansion research; neither source checked names them, they only say to use stable weights.
Two dumbbells, rowing alternately, logged like an alternating curl (bilateral, two implements). Whether reps count each arm or each pair is not settled.
